newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Jan budget surplus down from year ago.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Jan budget surplus down from year ago.

text.p: The government posted a budget surplus of $13.36 billion in January, the Treasury Department said on Monday, down from a surplus of $19.46 billion in January 1996.
This year's January surplus followed a revised surplus in December of $18.82 billion, which previously was reported as a surplus of $19.36 billion.
Total government spending in January was $137.35 billion, up from $123.54 billion in January 1996 and up from $129.67 billion in December.
Income from all sources, primarily taxes, increased to $150.72 billion in January from $143 billion in January 1996. In December, income totaled $148.49 billion.
In the first four months of fiscal 1997, which ends on Sept 30, the cumulative deficit has risen to $45.95 billion from $36.29 billion in the comparable first four months of fiscal 1996.
The Clinton administration has forecast a budget deficit of $125.59 billion for all of fiscal 1997, up from $107.01 billion in fiscal 1996.

During December, the government's income from personal taxes grew to $87.24 billion from $59.42 billion a month earlier in December. But corporate income tax receipts were down to $4.81 billion from $38.96 billion in December, when many corporations are required to make quarterly tax payments.
